# SBK Techno status page

The public service status page for `status.ia.sbktechno.com`: its page source, the `status.json` schema and validation, and its deterministic build. The platform host publishes the live document locally and the Caddy edge serves it; this repository never publishes a heartbeat, and its CI is validate-only.

## What the site is

A static public site served at `https://status.ia.sbktechno.com/` by the SBK Caddy edge.
It uses plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with no external runtime dependency: no
framework, third-party font, remote image, analytics, cookie, or browser storage.

The platform host publishes `status.json` at the site root on its systemd timer. The
publisher probes the public surfaces, writes the document and a signed receipt locally,
and the edge serves the document beside the release tree. The page reads only that public
file. It never calls the private platform, the portal, or the AI gateway.

The committed HTML carries a build-time snapshot: the overall state, the component rows,
the incidents, the exact `generated_at`, and a marker saying the snapshot may no longer be
current. A visitor without JavaScript sees the published status instead of a fallback that
says nothing is displayed. The snapshot is bound to the exact `status.json` bytes by
digest, so it cannot outlive or overstate the heartbeat it was rendered from.

French is the default language. English is available with the `FR | EN` switch. The choice
is kept in memory and can be shared as `?lang=en`; the page uses no browser storage.

This is not the documentation site. Documentation is internal staff documentation served
by Caddy at `https://ia.sbktechno.com/docs`.

## Hosting and delivery

The site is served by the owned Caddy edge from host state under `/var/lib/sbk/status`:
pages from `current`, content-hashed assets from `shared` first, and the live
`status.json` from the status root beside the release tree. The platform owns the site
block, the shared security header owner, and the cache policy. HTML revalidates,
`status.json` is `no-store`, and a filename carrying a 12 to 64 character content hash is
`public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.

`scripts/deploy/status.sh` builds a deterministic artifact from the status manifests,
requires a gate-attested platform commit, and hands it to the host installer. The host
publishes shared assets before the swap, writes a release record, swaps `current` in one
rename, verifies the result, and restores the previous release on failure. Rollback and
finalize are explicit modes. A shared asset tree keeps old hashed names addressable for
the immutable window, and a deploy never replaces the live document that the publisher
writes beside the tree.

## Brand and shared assets

The site is an SBK-operated surface, so it uses the same web brand system as the operator
portal and the internal documentation. The brand repository's `assets.json` is the single
owner of the logical web assets, and `assets/web/manifest.json` maps each logical name to a
content-hashed file, digest, media type, and byte size. This repository never copies that
brand list: `brand.manifest.json` is generated by the platform, and `site.manifest.json`
records only the four site assets this repository generates.

The graphite header renders the approved `logo-reverse.svg` unchanged, at its intrinsic
284x118 aspect ratio. Its width comes from the brand's `--sbk-logo-header` token (112 px,
height auto), so the status page does not define its own header size. This is a recorded
deviation from the brand guideline's 240 px minimum: the shared provider shell token is
112 px, and the status page follows the token rather than inventing a client-logo
exemption. Revisit the deviation with the brand owner before changing the asset.

The footer uses the published `icon-color.svg` on a `--sbk-text` plate: the brand blue
measures 2.92:1 directly on the `#080A0F` canvas, 5.99:1 on the plate, and the plate
separates from the canvas at 17.47:1. The header lockup is the brand's logotype, so WCAG
1.4.11's logotype exemption applies; the validator records that one exemption and requires
the exact approved fills `#FFFFFF` and `#2255BC`, a white wordmark at 4.5:1, the recorded
blue ratio on the rendered surface, and the header size from `--sbk-logo-header`. A
recolour or a surface change fails until it is re-approved.

`cmd/brandlint` is the design gate for every SBK-operated surface. It rejects raw colours,
literal font stacks, external stylesheet imports, missing shell markers, unresolved
placeholders, digest or size drift, and a published asset that a page does not reference.
Client apps are exempt.

## Rendering and manifests

`templates/index.html` and `templates/404.html` are the source. They reference brand assets
with `{{asset:<logical-name>}}` placeholders and site assets with
`{{site:<logical-name>}}` placeholders. `make brand` runs `cmd/genstatus` from the platform
checkout, then the site renderer and the retention gate:

- `cmd/genstatus` resolves every brand placeholder from the brand manifest and fails on an
  unknown name, an unresolved asset placeholder, or a literal hashed brand filename. It
  runs with `-brand-only`, so it writes the hashed brand assets and `brand.manifest.json`
  but leaves the pages to this repository's renderer.
- `scripts/build_site.py` resolves the site placeholders to content-hashed names, writes
  `site.manifest.json`, generates the print palette from the brand light tokens, and
  renders the snapshot from the exact `status.json` bytes.
- `scripts/prune_assets.py` records newly retired generated files in
  `asset-retention.json` and deletes files whose seven-day retention window has expired.
  `make brand-check` fails when an unmanifested file has no record or its window is
  overdue.

Never edit the root `index.html`, `404.html`, hashed `styles.css` copies,
`site.manifest.json`, `asset-retention.json`, the hashed brand assets, or
`brand.manifest.json` by hand. Change the template, the site source, the document, or the
brand repository and run `make brand`. The Caddy site block, the response headers, and the
cache policy are platform artifacts; this repository keeps none of them.

## Presentation

The public board is a graphite surface (`data-theme="dark"`). It opens with a text status
word in the status colour, a monospaced read time, and a compact inline-SVG vitals
instrument on the right. The instrument is decorative and `aria-hidden`; its arcs and
counts mirror the component board, which is the accessible source of the same facts. The
component rows and the incident timeline are separated by hairlines rather than cards.

`presentation()` in `status-model.js` is the single owner of every visible decision. It
returns exactly one mode, `loading`, `fresh`, `stale`, or `error`, and exactly one banner,
`null`, `stale`, or `error`. The renderer does not combine the payload, the error flag, and
freshness by itself, so the headline, the rows, the vitals count, and the notice cannot
disagree. At most one notice sits above the hero.

- `loading`: a read is in flight. On first load the build-time snapshot stays on screen
  instead; a short bounded read window retries quietly, and the error view appears only
  after that window ends.
- `fresh`: the publisher's confirmed status and summary are shown.
- `stale`: a missing, empty, future, expired, or aged heartbeat shows an unknown state, the
  last signal, the last read, and the source link. It never claims the service is down.
- `error`: one error notice with one retry action, no rows, no vitals, and no counts. A
  failed read never shows the stale notice at the same time.

The static HTML is a real snapshot, not a placeholder. At build time `scripts/build_site.py`
renders the headline, component rows, incident journal, `generated_at`, and snapshot
marker into the page from the exact committed `status.json` bytes. The body records the
document's SHA-256 and the instant the freshness rules were applied;
`scripts/validate_status.py` re-renders the same document and rejects a page whose digest,
instant, headline, rows, counts, summary, or stale notice disagree.

With JavaScript disabled the page keeps the snapshot, the snapshot check time, and the
vitals, hides the language switch while reserving its space, and links `status.json` in the
`<noscript>` note and the footer. With JavaScript enabled, the page refreshes every 60
seconds and when the tab becomes visible.

Print and forced-colours light mode cannot use the reverse lockup: its white wordmark
disappears on a light sheet. Both blocks hide that asset and show the published one-colour
`icon-color.svg` with a text `SBK Techno` wordmark. The print palette is generated from the
brand's light tokens and re-measured by the validator.

## Heartbeat and freshness

The platform `cmd/statuspublisher` probes the public surfaces, writes `status.json`
atomically to the host status root, and signs the exact bytes with HMAC-SHA256 into
`status.published.json`. The publisher is the only writer of the live document; this
repository owns the schema and the committed seed. The systemd publisher timer and the
freshness timer are installed and enabled, and the published document and receipt are
`0640 sbk-status:sbk-portal`.

The status systemd unit loads the one HMAC credential from the platform's secret
directory, and the publisher reads it from `$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY`. It is the only
status credential, the publication path has no other secret and no repository write, and
this repository never handles the key. Never commit the key value.

Freshness rules:

- `generated_at` is null, empty, or unparseable: no heartbeat. `overall` and every
  component must be `unknown`; the validator rejects a healthy claim without a heartbeat.
- `generated_at` is more than 5 minutes in the future: invalid.
- `expires_at` is in the past, or `generated_at` is older than 15 minutes: stale.
- Any missing, empty, future, expired, or aged heartbeat forces the headline, every
  component row, and the vitals signal count to `unknown`, shows no per-row verification
  time, and opens with the stale notice above the hero.
- A failed fetch renders the unavailable view even when a previous payload is retained:
  no rows, no vitals, and no counts from the old document.

The publisher writes `generated_at` and `expires_at` in UTC; `expires_at` is at most 15
minutes after `generated_at`. Incidents stay operator-owned: the publisher copies them
from its configured incident file and never invents or resolves one.

## Status document

`status.json` is schema version 1. The top level requires `version`, `generated_at`,
`expires_at`, `overall`, `summary_fr`, `summary_en`, `components`, and `incidents`.
A component requires a unique `id`, `label_fr`, `label_en`, `status`, `detail_fr`, and
`detail_en`. An incident requires a unique `id`, `status`, `title_fr`, `title_en`,
`started_at`, `updated_at`, `summary_fr`, and `summary_en`.

`generated_at` and `expires_at` are UTC ISO 8601 timestamps. They are both null or both
set, and the document lifetime is at most 15 minutes. A heartbeat more than 5 minutes in
the future is rejected. When the timestamps are null, `overall` and every component must
be `unknown`; a document cannot claim a confirmed state without a heartbeat. Components
are rendered in JSON order, and active incidents are rendered before resolved ones.

| Value | French label | English label |
|---|---|---|
| `operational` | Opérationnel | Operational |
| `degraded` | Dégradé | Degraded |
| `partial_outage` | Panne partielle | Partial outage |
| `major_outage` | Panne majeure | Major outage |
| `maintenance` | Maintenance | Maintenance |
| `unknown` | Inconnu | Unknown |

Incident status values:

| Value | French label | English label |
|---|---|---|
| `investigating` | Enquête en cours | Investigating |
| `identified` | Cause identifiée | Identified |
| `monitoring` | Sous surveillance | Monitoring |
| `resolved` | Résolu | Resolved |

Every incident requires all fields, and `updated_at` is not before `started_at`.

## Post-deploy verification

`make verify-published URL=https://status.ia.sbktechno.com/` proves that the live site is
the artifact this repository built and that the live document is fresh. It needs the
deployed origin, so it is not part of `make validate`. It is read-only, bounded, and made
for a local run after the edge release. It verifies that `/status.json` is live with schema
version 1, that the document is fresh under the 15-minute rule, that `/` and `/404.html`
match the built pages, that every referenced asset is manifest-owned and matches its
digest, byte size, and media type, and that the page digest and snapshot instant agree
with the committed document the page was built from.

It also checks that a conditional request returns 304 with an empty body, that no response
sets a cookie, and that a directory path is not a listing. The platform edge owns the
response headers and cache policy, and the platform edge tests prove them.

Exit status is `0` when every check passes, `1` when a published check fails, and `2` for a
usage error. The offline verifier suite runs a loopback fixture origin built from the real
site output and covers a missing asset, stale digest, bad schema, stale or future
document, 304 with a body, directory listing, `Set-Cookie`, wrong content type, and a
rebuilt asset name the old origin does not serve. No test reaches the network.

## Local preview

Serve the repository root from a local HTTP server:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`. Do not open `index.html` through `file://`: browsers block
the `status.json` fetch for local files, so the page shows its error state.

## Local checks

```sh
make validate
make brand
make brand-check
make cls-check
make verify-published URL=https://status.ia.sbktechno.com/
```

`make cls-check` is the browser layout and cache gate. It needs Playwright and its
Chromium build, which CI does not install:

```sh
python3 -m pip install --user playwright
python3 -m playwright install chromium
```

It serves the built site from a loopback origin, holds `status.json` until the first
paint, and proves at 1440x900 and 390x844 that CLS stays below 0.05, that the hero and
board do not move when the read resolves, and that hashed assets carry the immutable
header.

`make validate` needs the platform and brand checkouts. By default it reads
`.toolchain/platform` and `.toolchain/brand`; that directory is Git ignored. Create the
links once, or pass `make validate PLATFORM=/path/to/platform BRAND=/path/to/brand`. A
missing checkout fails with the exact path and the override to set.

`make validate` expands `GATE_TARGETS` from the Makefile: the document and site validator,
the unit suites, the workflow and Makefile contract test, `brand-check`, `render-check`,
`assets-check`, the platform `statuscheck`, `governance-check`, the pinned `actionlint`,
the pre-push hook checks, and `cmd/brandlint`. The workflow invokes the same target; it
keeps no second list of checks. It never publishes: local publication belongs to the
platform host.

## Security and privacy

- `index.html` and `404.html` carry the same strict CSP, generated once from
  `templates/csp.txt`: `default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; font-src
  'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`.
  JavaScript and CSS live in separate files, with no inline scripts or inline styles.
- The meta policy deliberately omits `frame-ancestors`; browsers ignore that directive in
  a meta CSP. The edge sends it as a response header.
- There are no secrets, cookies, browser storage, analytics, service workers, beacons, or
  external assets. The `status.json` fetch uses `credentials: "omit"`.
- Everything published in this repository and in `status.json` is public. Never put
  private platform data, client data, tokens, or internal URLs in the status file.

The edge sends the response headers a meta tag cannot carry:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Content-Security-Policy` | The `templates/csp.txt` policy plus `frame-ancestors 'none'`. |
| `Cache-Control` (HTML) | `public, max-age=600, must-revalidate` |
| `Cache-Control` (hashed assets) | `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` |
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` |
| `Referrer-Policy` | `no-referrer` |
| `X-Frame-Options` | `DENY` |
